title: Saxe-Altenburg
capsule: Saxe-Altenburg was a small Ernestine Wettin duchy in Thuringia centred on Altenburg, reconstituted in 1826 when the Saxe-Gotha-Altenburg line became extinct and territories were redistributed among the Ernestine branches. Covering only 1,323 km² with a population of roughly 207,000, it was one of the smallest members of the German Confederation; Duke Joseph (r. 1834–1868) navigated 1848 without revolution by granting a revised constitution. The duchy joined the North German Confederation in 1866 and the German Empire in 1871; Duke Ernst I abdicated on 13 November 1918 during the German Revolution, and the territory merged into the Free State of Thuringia in 1920.
